description: Hi, I am Ariel Sion. Our team is currently looking for new members to tackle a challenge focused on software and human exploration. We are seeking individuals with strong skills in software development, data analysis, and user interface design to help build systems that gather and evaluate physiological indicators. If you have a background in biomedical engineering or experience creating tools that allow users to monitor and act on health data, you will be a perfect fit for our project.
summary:
Astronauts face significant physical and psychological health challenges during long-duration space missions, including the effects of microgravity, radiation, isolation, and sleep disturbances.

ATLAS is an intelligent health monitoring software platform designed to support astronauts' well-being by integrating physical and psychological assessments into a single, user-friendly interface.

The platform organizes physiological indicators such as heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation, and blood test results, considering both daily measurements and periodic medical evaluations.

For psychological monitoring, ATLAS incorporates scientifically established assessments such as PVT, AMS, and BDI-II. Through ATLAS Companion, a virtual voice assistant, astronauts can complete guided assessments in a more natural, accessible, and engaging way.

By centralizing health records, visualizing trends, and identifying potentially concerning changes, ATLAS aims to support early intervention and informed medical decision-making.
details:
ATLAS is a software platform designed to support the physical and psychological health monitoring of astronauts during long-duration space missions. It brings health information together in one accessible environment through two interconnected modules.

Physical Health Module

This module allows astronauts to visualize important health indicators, including heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation, sleep patterns, radiation exposure, and medical test results. Its interactive 3D Body Twin provides a visual representation of the human body, allowing users to explore health indicators, review historical records, and identify values that may require attention.

Psychological Health Module

This module incorporates PVT, AMS, and BDI-II assessments to monitor attention, mood, fatigue-related performance, and depressive symptoms. It also includes a conversational virtual assistant that allows astronauts to complete psychological assessments through natural voice interactions, making the experience more comfortable and engaging.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The main benefit of ATLAS is integrating physical and psychological health information into a single platform. It considers that some measurements must be performed daily, while others, such as blood tests, are conducted periodically. This helps organize health records, visualize changes over time, and support medical follow-up.

Our creative approach combines an interactive 3D human model, conversational artificial intelligence, and centralized health monitoring in one platform. The project is inspired by NASA's Human Research Program and research conducted in spaceflight analog environments, including the Mars-500 study.

Tools and Development

ATLAS was developed as a software-only project. Figma was used for interface design, and simulated data is used to demonstrate the prototype. No dedicated hardware is required.

Our intended impact is to contribute to safer and more human-centered space exploration by helping astronauts and medical teams better understand and monitor astronaut health, even when Earth is millions of kilometers away.
